title: B2 · L1 — Third conditional
description: Tercer condicional: 'if + past perfect, would have + participio'. Se usa para hablar de situaciones pasadas irreales y sus consecuencias hipotéticas.

questions.prompt: Situación: te disculpas con tu jefe por llegar tarde a la reunión de las 8.
questions.question: Complete: 'If I ___ the alarm, I wouldn't have missed the flight.'
options: had heard
would hear
would have heard
heard
questions.explanation: El tercer condicional siempre lleva 'past perfect' en la cláusula del 'if' y 'would have + participio' en el resultado. Error clásico de hispanohablante: poner 'would have' en las DOS cláusulas por espejo con 'habría/habría' del español. En inglés estándar 'would have' NUNCA va después de 'if'.
examples: If I had heard the alarm, I would've caught the 6 a.m. flight. → excusa en el trabajo
She wouldn't have panicked if she had checked her calendar the night before.

questions.prompt: Situación: comentas con un colega por qué no llegasteis a la reunión.
questions.question: Choose the correct third conditional:
options: If we had left earlier, we would catch the train.
If we would have left earlier, we would have caught the train.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
If we left earlier, we had caught the train.
questions.explanation: La fórmula fija es: 'if + had + participio, would have + participio'. Las otras opciones mezclan tiempos de otros condicionales (segundo o primero). 'If + would have' se oye en inglés americano coloquial, pero se considera incorrecto en escritura y exámenes tipo B2 First.
examples: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the 7:15. → post-mortem en la oficina
Honestly, if I had known there'd be traffic, I would've taken the metro.

questions.statement: El tercer condicional se refiere a acontecimientos pasados reales que sucedieron.
questions.explanation: FALSO. El tercer condicional describe siempre lo CONTRARIO de lo que ocurrió. Si digo 'If I had studied, I would have passed', significa que NO estudié y NO aprobé. Es la típica gramática del 'hubiera/habría' del español para arrepentimientos, críticas o alivios.
examples: If I had known, I would have called you. → implica: no lo supe, no llamé
She would have won the promotion if she hadn't quit. → implica: sí renunció, no ganó

questions.text: If she had told me the truth, I wouldn't have been so upset.
questions.explanation: Speech connectado: 'would have' casi siempre se reduce a 'would've' /ˈwʊdəv/, y 'wouldn't have' suena como 'wouldn't-əv'. El 'had' inicial se pronuncia débil (/əd/), casi pegado al pronombre: 'if-she-əd told me'. Confundir 'would've' con 'would of' (falso amigo escrito) es un error muy común.
examples: If she had told me sooner, I would've rearranged my whole week.
I wouldn't have been so angry if you had just explained. → tono de reproche

questions.prompt: Le explicas a un amigo por qué no fuiste a su cumple.
questions.question: Which sentence expresses regret about a past action?
options: If I have more time, I will visit you.
If I had more time, I would visit you.
If I had had more time, I would have visited you.
If I have had more time, I would visit you.
questions.explanation: El doble 'had had' asusta pero es correcto: el primer 'had' es el auxiliar del past perfect y el segundo el participio de 'have' (tener). Sólo el tercer condicional puro ('had had... would have + PP') expresa arrepentimiento por algo que no hicimos. Las otras opciones hablan del futuro o del presente hipotético.
examples: If I had had more money back then, I would have travelled around Asia. → arrepentimiento
If he had had the guts to speak up in the meeting, they would have listened to him.

questions.statement: 'If I would have known' es gramaticalmente correcto en inglés estándar.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Aunque muchos nativos americanos lo dicen ('If I woulda known...'), es incorrecto en inglés estándar y te bajará la nota en cualquier examen B2/C1. La forma correcta es 'If I had known'. Truco mnemotécnico: 'would' es el resultado, no la condición — así que nunca va detrás de 'if'.
examples: Correct: If I had known you were vegetarian, I would've ordered differently.
Incorrect: If I would have known... → suena natural en EE. UU. hablado, pero es error escrito

questions.prompt: Empareja cada cláusula 'if' con su resultado hipotético lógico:

pairs.right: they would have won the match.

pairs.left: If I hadn't taken that job,
pairs.right: I would never have met her.
if we had brought a map.
I would have given you a hand.

questions.explanation: Todas comparten la misma estructura: past perfect + would have + participio. Fíjate que el orden es intercambiable: 'If..., would have' (con coma) o 'would have... if' (sin coma). El significado no cambia, sólo el énfasis: cuando el 'if' va primero, se enfatiza la condición.
examples: If you had told me, I would've brought wine. → énfasis en la condición
I would've helped if you had just asked. → énfasis en el resultado / tono levemente resentido

questions.prompt: Un amigo se lamenta de no haber ido a un concierto agotado.
questions.question: Complete: 'You ___ the concert if you had bought tickets earlier.'
options: would enjoy
would have enjoyed
will enjoy
enjoyed
questions.explanation: El resultado del tercer condicional lleva SIEMPRE 'would/could/might have + participio pasado'. 'Would enjoy' pertenece al segundo condicional (presente/futuro hipotético) y 'will enjoy' al primero (futuro real). El pasado imposible sólo se expresa con 'would have + PP'.
examples: You would've loved the encore — she played her acoustic set. → mostrar empatía
They might have got backstage passes if they had arrived earlier.

questions.target: If I had studied harder at university, I would have found a better job.
questions.explanation: Frase típica de reflexión personal (entrevista, coffee chat, terapia). En hablado 'would have' se reduce a 'would've' /wʊdəv/ y el 'had' de 'I had studied' pierde peso — suena casi como 'if-I'd-studied'. Nativos añaden hedging: 'Maybe...', 'I sometimes think...' para no sonar demasiado autocrítico.
examples: Honestly, if I'd studied harder, I would've landed a scholarship. → confesión con amigo
Sometimes I think if she'd chosen medicine, she would've earned way more.

questions.prompt: Analizas con un colega qué habría podido pasar si hubierais reaccionado antes.
questions.question: Which modal alternative to 'would have' expresses possibility (not certainty)?
options: must have
might have
should have
will have
questions.explanation: En el tercer condicional podemos sustituir 'would have' por otros modales para matizar: 'might/could have' = posibilidad hipotética; 'should have' = crítica u obligación no cumplida; 'must have' = deducción sobre el pasado, no hipótesis. Al escoger el modal cambias el matiz emocional de la frase.
examples: If we had left earlier, we might have caught the train. → posibilidad, no seguridad
She could have won the pitch if she'd been more focused. → capacidad hipotética

questions.statement: El tercer condicional se usa a menudo para expresar arrepentimiento, crítica o alivio sobre el pasado.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Los tres usos emocionales típicos son: arrepentimiento ('I would have called you'), crítica velada ('You could have warned me') y alivio ('We could have been killed!'). El tono lo marca el modal escogido: 'would' es neutro/reflexivo, 'could/might' añade posibilidad, 'should' añade juicio.
examples: Regret: If only I had listened to her advice back then. → autocrítica suave
Relief: If we hadn't left the hotel when we did, we would've been caught in the earthquake.

questions.text: He wouldn't have crashed the car if he hadn't been checking his phone.
questions.explanation: Connected speech: 'wouldn't have' se fusiona a 'wouldn't-əv' y 'hadn't been' suena como 'hadn't-bin' con schwa. Nota el past perfect continuo ('had been checking') para acciones interrumpidas — es muy común al explicar accidentes: enfatiza que la acción estaba EN CURSO justo antes.
examples: She wouldn't have failed the interview if she hadn't been so nervous.
We wouldn't have missed the exit if the GPS hadn't been glitching. → excusa en el coche

questions.prompt: Redactas un email formal disculpándote con un cliente.
questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct inversion (formal register):
options: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
If had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
I had known about the traffic, would have left earlier.
Had known I about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
questions.explanation: En registro formal (correspondencia, discursos, informes) omitimos 'if' e invertimos auxiliar y sujeto: 'Had I known...'. Suena elegante y literario, pero fuera de lugar en un chat con amigos. Nativos lo usan en emails, discursos o novelas; en el bar dirían 'If I'd known...'.
examples: Had she realised the impact, she would have apologised immediately. → informe interno
Had we been informed sooner, we would have taken the necessary precautions.

questions.target: Had I known you were coming, I would have prepared something special for dinner.
questions.explanation: Estructura formal con inversión, típica en discursos o al recibir a alguien inesperado con un toque teatral/cortés. En hablado el 'Had' inicial recibe énfasis y 'would have' se reduce a 'would've'. Un nativo lo dice medio en broma en casa; en el bar diría simplemente 'If I'd known you were coming...'.
examples: Had I known you were vegan, I would've made the risotto instead. → anfitrión formal-cálido
Had we been warned about the delay, we would've rebooked. → queja educada en atención al cliente

questions.prompt: Un amigo reflexiona sobre qué carrera eligió.
questions.question: Which is a mixed conditional (past condition → present result)?
options: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
If I studied medicine, I would be a doctor.
If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor.
If I study medicine, I will be a doctor.
questions.explanation: El condicional mixto salta entre tiempos: 'past perfect' en la condición (algo que no pasó en el pasado) + 'would + infinitivo' en el resultado (consecuencia presente). La palabra clave es a menudo 'now' o 'today'. La opción C es tercer condicional puro; B es segundo condicional; D es primer condicional.
examples: If I had accepted that offer in 2020, I would be living in Berlin right now. → reflexión vital
If she hadn't quit her job, she would still be earning six figures. → cotilleo entre amigos
